In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EGFR testing should be performed by two methods (IHC and FISH or PCR) and the results should be correlated with the clinical outcome of the patients to validate the test results.
EGFR abnormalities should be tested in patients with pulmonary neoplasms by more than one method, and that the results of each test should not be interpreted as the only one.
the results of IHC and PCR are not comparable to each other and that IHC should not be used as a single method to detect EGFR abnormalities in pulmonary adenocarcins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EGFR testing should be done with two different methods, such as IHC and PCR.
the EGFR testing should not be done as a single method, but as a panel of two or three different tests.

PCR is a less sensitive test than IHC or FISH and that it should not be used alone as the sole method for EGFR testing.
